ncmapi-rs

NetEase Cloud Music API for Rust. `NcmClient` is the sole public SDK entry point. `NcmApi` remains only as a deprecated alias for a short migration window. ### Usage ```toml [dependencies] ncmapi = "1" tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] } ``` ```rust use ncmapi::{NcmClient, SearchKind, SearchQuery}; #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> std::result::Result<(), Box> { let api = NcmClient::builder().build()?; let response = api .discovery() .search(SearchQuery::new("mota")?.kind(SearchKind::Artist)) .await?; for song in response.body.result.songs { println!("{} — {}", song.id, song.name); } Ok(()) } ``` ### Architecture The public surface is intentionally small: - `client.discovery()` searches the catalogue. - `client.library()` reads tracks and stream URLs. - `client.profile()` reads account and user information. Each service accepts value types and returns an `ApiResponse` whose body is a stable domain model. Services create immutable request plans; `NcmClient` delegates them to an internal transport that owns protocol encryption, cookies, caching, and HTTP I/O. This keeps the domain layer deterministic and lets the test suite exercise it without accessing the external music service. `1.0` removes the former `NcmApi` endpoint methods. Migrate calls to a focused service, for example `client.discovery().search(SearchQuery::new("mota")?)`. ### Contribute If you think this package useful, please do make pull requests. Run the deterministic test suite with `cargo test`. The SDK deliberately does not run external-service checks in its normal development workflow. ### License [MIT](LICENSE) ===SDK=== use std::{path::PathBuf, sync::Arc, time::Duration}; use crate::{ TResult, transport::{HttpTransportBuilder, RequestPlan, Response, Transport}, }; /// The public entry point for the Netease Cloud Music SDK. /// /// Construct it with [`NcmClient::builder`]. Endpoint APIs are exposed as /// focused services, while this type owns the shared transport boundary. pub struct NcmClient { transport: Arc, } /// Builds an [`NcmClient`] from explicit infrastructure choices. #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct NcmClientBuilder { cache_enabled: bool, cache_ttl: Duration, persist_cookies: bool, cookie_path: PathBuf, } impl Default for NcmClientBuilder { fn default() -> Self { Self { cache_enabled: true, cache_ttl: Duration::from_secs(3 * 60), persist_cookies: true, cookie_path: std::env::temp_dir().join("ncmapi-cookies"), } } } impl NcmClientBuilder { /// Disables or enables the short-lived response cache. pub fn cache(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.cache_enabled = enabled; self } /// Sets the lifetime of cached responses. pub fn cache_ttl(mut self, ttl: Duration) -> Self { self.cache_ttl = ttl; self } /// Chooses whether cookies received from the service are persisted. pub fn persist_cookies(mut self, enabled: bool) -> Self { self.persist_cookies = enabled; self } /// Sets the file used to persist cookies between client instances. pub fn cookie_path(mut self, path: impl Into) -> Self { self.cookie_path = path.into(); self } /// Creates the client and reports invalid local configuration eagerly. pub fn build(self) -> TResult { let transport = HttpTransportBuilder::new(&self.cookie_path)? .cache(self.cache_enabled) .cache_ttl(self.cache_ttl) .persist_cookies(self.persist_cookies) .build()?; Ok(NcmClient { transport: Arc::new(transport), }) } } impl NcmClient { pub fn builder() -> NcmClientBuilder { NcmClientBuilder::default() } pub(crate) async fn execute(&self, request: RequestPlan) -> TResult { self.transport.execute(request).await } #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn with_transport(transport: Arc) -> Self { Self { transport } } }

# lekima — Product Design

> NetEase Cloud Music in your terminal. Vim-first, agent-native.

Status: **Draft for v0.1** · Owner: @benmooo · Rewrite of the archived Go project
[`benmooo/lekima`](https://github.com/benmooo/lekima)

---

## 1. Why rewrite

The original lekima (Go, 2018–2022, archived) proved the idea: a terminal
NetEase Cloud Music client that feels like a vim buffer. It also accumulated the
usual debt of a 1.6k-line single-package program:

| Original constraint | Consequence today |
| --- | --- |
| `termui`/`termbox`, no layout engine | No resizing story, no real widgets, one theme |
| Global mutable `Lekima` struct, `panic` on errors | Any API hiccup kills the player; untestable |
| `faiface/beep` + full-body MP3 download | Long delay before playback, no seeking strategy |
| Phone/password login only | Passwords on disk, no QR, no cookie reuse |
| No machine interface | Nothing can drive it except a human at a keyboard |
| Go API client (`benmooo/ncmapi`) | Not reusable from the Rust ecosystem |

The rewrite keeps the soul (keyboard-driven, fast, quiet) and fixes the
foundation: a layered Rust workspace, a long-lived player daemon, and a first
class machine interface.

## 2. Positioning

**One-liner:** the music player for people who already live in a terminal — and
for the agents working beside them.

**Not** a GUI music app, not a downloader, not a streaming aggregator. One
provider, done well, with a UI that never gets in the way.

### Target users

1. **Terminal-native developers** — vim/neovim/helix users, tmux dwellers, tiling
   WM users. They want to search, queue, and skip without leaving the keyboard.
2. **Code agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, scripts. They need a
   stable, documented, non-interactive command surface and JSON output.
3. **The author** — a maintainer of `ncmapi-rs` who wants the crate exercised by
   a real, demanding consumer.

### Jobs to be done

- “Play something I like without opening a browser or a 300 MB Electron app.”
- “Keep playing while I work; let me skip with one key.”
- “While I code, have the agent put on my daily playlist and turn it down.”
- “I’m SSH’d into a box; can I still control the music on this machine?”
- “Script it: play my liked playlist at 09:00 on weekdays.”

## 3. Product principles

1. **Keyboard is the first-class input.** Every action has a key. No feature is
   mouse-only. Keys follow vim semantics (`j/k`, `g/G`, `/`, `:` , counts).
2. **Fast by default.** First playback in under 30 s from a cold install; key
   latency under 16 ms; the TUI never blocks on the network.
3. **Quiet and legible.** No splash screens, no ads, no notification spam.
   Errors are one line plus an actionable hint.
4. **Composable.** A daemon owns playback; the TUI and the CLI are equal clients.
   Anything the TUI can do, a shell can do.
5. **Honest about state.** “Paused”, “buffering”, “no stream available (VIP)” are
   distinct states, not a generic error.
6. **Privacy and safety.** Credentials never appear in logs or process args;
   untrusted catalogue text is sanitized before it reaches a terminal.
7. **Provider respect.** No DRM circumvention, no bulk downloading. Use the
   provider’s official play URLs and honour its session model.

## 4. Scope

### v0.1 — “it plays” (current milestone)

| Area | Included |
| --- | --- |
| Session | Reuse an existing browser cookie (`lekima login --cookie`), `whoami`, `logout`; QR login in v0.2 |
| Catalogue | Search tracks; track metadata; playlist listing and playlist tracks |
| Playback | Play/pause/resume/stop, next/previous, seek, volume, mute, repeat off/all/one, autoplay next |
| Queue | View, enqueue (append or “play next”), clear, jump |
| TUI | Now-playing bar with progress, track table, sidebar (playlists), search prompt, help overlay, vim keybindings, resize-safe layout |
| CLI | Every action above as a subcommand, `--json`, stable exit codes, daemon autostart |
| Ops | `doctor`, `daemon start/stop/status`, log file, `LEKIMA_CONFIG_DIR` for hermetic use |

### v0.2 — “it feels finished”

QR login, lyrics pane (synced), daily recommendations, personal FM, liked
playlist, like/unlike, playlist search, mouse-optional scroll, themes,
`NO_COLOR`, `lekima mcp` stdio server, client-side response of live events
(push protocol) instead of polling.

### Later

Comments pane (“hot comments” was in the original), cloud disk, toplists,
downloads for offline cache, MPRIS/D-Bus + macOS Now Playing integration,
desktop notifications, Last.fm scrobbling, multiple profiles, plugin hooks,
`lekima serve --http` for LAN control, WASM/embedded agent tooling.

### Explicit non-goals

- GUI/TUI parity with the web player’s social features.
- Downloading copyrighted tracks for redistribution.
- Bypassing regional or VIP restrictions.
- Reimplementing the NetEase recommendation stack.

## 5. Experience

### 5.1 Screen model

```
┌ lekima ──────────────────────────────────────────────── ◉ 320kbps  12:04 ┐
│ ▍Now Playing                                                            │
│   Bohemian Rhapsody · Queen · A Night at the Opera                      │
│   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━──────────── 1:42 / 5:55      vol 70%  repeat off   │
├─ Library ────────────┬─ Tracks ─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▾ My playlists (12)  │   #  TITLE                 ARTIST        TIME     │
│   • Late night       │   1  mota                  Zhang        3:12  ▶  │
│   • Focus            │   2  ...                                               │
│ ▸ Daily              │                                                       │
│ ▸ FM                 │                                                       │
├──────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ NORMAL  j/k move  ⏎ play  space pause  / search  ? help        queue 12  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Header / now-playing**: title, artist, album, progress, volume, repeat,
  shuffle, and the resolved bitrate. Updates at 4 Hz while playing.
- **Sidebar**: sections — My playlists, Daily recommendations, Personal FM,
  Search results. Collapsible, navigable.
- **Main pane**: a table for tracks (index, title, artist, album, duration,
  state marker) or a list for playlists.
- **Status bar**: mode (NORMAL / SEARCH / HELP), contextual hints, queue length,
  transient messages (“queued 3 tracks”, errors in red for 4 s).
- **Overlays**: search prompt (`/`), command line (`:`), help (`?`), confirm
  dialogs for destructive actions.

### 5.2 Keymap (v0.1)

Global — `q`/`Ctrl-c` quit, `?` help, `/` search, `:` command line,
`Tab` cycle focus, `Esc` close overlay/cancel.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `j` / `k` | Move down / up |
| `Ctrl-d` / `Ctrl-u` | Half-page down / up |
| `g` / `G` | Top / bottom |
| `5j`, `12G` (v0.2) | Count prefix |
| `Enter` | Play selection (or open playlist/section) |
| `Space` | Pause / resume |
| `n` / `p` | Next / previous track |
| `+` / `-` | Volume up / down 5% |
| `m` | Mute toggle |
| `r` | Cycle repeat off → all → one |
| `s` | Toggle shuffle (v0.2) |
| `a` | Append selection to queue |
| `A` | Play next (insert after current) |
| `x` | Remove selected queued track (with confirm) |
| `l` / `h` | Seek forward / back 10 s (also `→`/`←`) |
| `1`…`4` | Focus sidebar / main / queue / lyrics (v0.2) |
| `Q` | Show queue pane |
| `y` | Yank track URL/ID to clipboard (v0.2) |
| `P` | Toggle provider panel? (removed — `P` in the original was play mode) |

> Compatibility note: the archived app used `o`/`Enter` to expand the playlist
> tree. We keep `o` as “open” alias for muscle memory.

### 5.3 Interaction states

- **Empty**: “Nothing queued. Press `/` to search.”
- **Loading**: spinner in the header, skeleton rows, keys stay responsive.
- **No stream**: “This track has no playable stream (VIP or region).” The queue
  skips automatically after 2 s unless `--strict`.
- **Offline / provider down**: banner “offline — showing cached library”;
  playback of already-resolved URLs continues.
- **Unauthenticated**: browsing works where the provider allows it; play shows
  “login required” with the exact command to run.

### 5.4 Accessibility & terminal hygiene

- Every control is reachable by keyboard; no key requires a modifier combo that
  terminals commonly swallow.
- Colour is never the only signal (icons + text).
- `NO_COLOR`, `LEKIMA_THEME=light|dark|none`, and a monochrome-safe theme.
- Alternate screen is configurable; on exit the terminal is always restored
  (panic-safe guard).
- Catalogue text is sanitized: C0/C1 control characters and OSC/CSI sequences
  are stripped before rendering, preventing terminal escape injection from
  playlist or track names.

## 6. Agent contract

This is a product feature, not an afterthought. Rules:

1. **Non-interactive by default.** No prompts, no pager, no alternate screen for
   non-TUI commands.
2. **Machine output.** `--json` on every command. JSON goes to stdout; logs and
   diagnostics go to stderr. One JSON object per invocation.
3. **Stable vocabulary.** Command names, error codes and JSON fields are
   versioned; breaking changes require a major bump and a deprecation cycle.
4. **Bounded time.** Every command completes or fails within 30 s unless the
   user asks for `--wait`.
5. **Discoverable.** `lekima capabilities --json` returns the command catalogue,
   argument schema and examples; `lekima schema` returns the JSON schema.
6. **Daemon transparent.** Read commands work without a daemon; playback
   commands autostart one (unless `--no-daemon`) and report the PID.
7. **No secrets in argv.** `lekima login` reads the cookie from stdin or a file,
   not `--cookie=<secret>` on the command line (the flag accepts `-` for stdin).

### Command surface (v0.1)

```
lekima tui                                  open the interactive player
lekima play [QUERY] [--id ID]... [--playlist ID] [--shuffle] [--json]
lekima pause | resume | toggle | stop
lekima next | prev | seek <1:23|83s|+10s|-10s>
lekima volume [LEVEL|+5|-5] [--mute|--unmute] [--json]
lekima queue [list] [--json]
lekima queue add <QUERY|--id ID>... [--next]
lekima queue clear
lekima search <QUERY> [--kind track|album|artist|playlist] [--limit N] [--json]
lekima playlist list [--json]
lekima playlist show <ID> [--json]
lekima lyrics [--id ID] [--json]           (v0.2)
lekima status [--json]
lekima login [--cookie-file PATH|-] [--qr] (--qr in v0.2)
lekima logout
lekima whoami [--json]
lekima daemon start|stop|status|logs
lekima doctor [--json]
lekima capabilities [--json]
lekima completions <shell>
```

### JSON envelope

```json
{ "ok": true, "data": { "status": "playing", "track": { "id": 123, "name": "…" } } }
```

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "unauthorized", "message": "run `lekima login`" } }
```

Error codes are the single source of truth and map 1:1 to the daemon’s IPC
`ErrorCode`: `bad_request`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`, `unsupported`,
`backend`, `playback`, `daemon`, `internal`.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Unexpected internal error |
| 2 | Invalid usage (clap) |
| 3 | `unauthorized` |
| 4 | `not_found` |
| 5 | `backend` (provider/network) |
| 6 | `playback` (audio device) |
| 7 | `daemon` (unreachable and could not autostart) |
| 8 | `unsupported` |

### Example agent transcripts

```console
$ lekima play "mota" --json
{"ok":true,"data":{"status":"playing","track":{"id":…,"name":"mota"},"queue_length":12}}

$ lekima volume +10 --json
{"ok":true,"data":{"volume":0.8,"muted":false}}

$ lekima status --json | jq -r .data.status
playing
```

Roadmap: `lekima mcp` exposes `play`, `pause`, `next`, `search`, `status` as MCP
tools for agents that prefer tool calls over shell.

## 7. Success criteria (v0.1)

- Cold install → first sound in < 30 s, documented in the README.
- TUI stays at ≥ 30 FPS while a search is in flight.
- 100% of TUI actions have a CLI equivalent (checked by a table-driven test).
- `lekima play … --json` works headless (no TTY) with the daemon running.
- Zero panics on malformed provider payloads (fuzz/property tests on mapping).
- Clean `cargo clippy -D warnings`, no `unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).
- Runs on macOS (arm64) and Linux (x86_64, Wayland/X11); Windows is best-effort.

## 8. Milestones

| Milestone | Contents | Exit criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M0 Skeleton** (done) | Workspace, domain, config, IPC, core player rules | `cargo test` green |
| **M1 Playback** | ncm adapter, rodio engine, daemon, CLI play/status | Sound from the CLI |
| **M2 TUI** | ratatui shell, keymap, search, queue, help | Daily-drivable |
| **M3 Agent surface** | JSON everywhere, capabilities, exit codes, doctor | Scripted demo passes |
| **M4 Provider completeness** | ncmapi-rs 1.1: QR login, playlist detail, lyrics, daily/FM | TUI feature parity with old app |
| **M5 Release** | Packaging, docs, CI matrix, 0.1.0 tag | Installable from crates.io + release binaries |

## 9. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NetEase changes signing/anti-bot | Playback breaks | Keep transport isolated in `ncmapi`; contract tests; fast releases |
| VIP/region restrictions on stream URLs | “No URL” for many tracks | Distinguish `unsupported` from `backend`; skip-with-notice; document |
| Audio backend differences (CoreAudio, ALSA, Pulse) | Silence/crash | rodio + device enumeration in `doctor`; `--audio-device`; integration test on CI |
| Terminal escape injection via metadata | Security | Sanitize all external strings (unit-tested) |
| Daemon/CLI version skew | Weird behaviour | Protocol version field; client refuses unknown major |
| Cookie theft | Account compromise | `0600` session file, no logging, permission check on startup |
| Scope creep (social features) | Never ships | Non-goals above; milestones |

## 10. Open questions

1. **Name.** The rewrite is called `lekima` for continuity; the binary is
   `lekima`. Confirm before the first publish (renaming a crate later is a
   breaking change).
2. **Default UI density.** Do we keep the original’s always-visible sidebar, or
   start in a single-pane “just the queue” mode?
3. **Comments pane.** Beloved in the original; expensive to maintain. v0.3?
4. **Lyrics rendering.** Synced highlighting requires a timed LRC parser — worth
   the dependency, or plain text first?
5. **Windows.** WSL only, or native named pipes in v1.0?

# lekima — System Design Status: **Draft for v0.1** · Companion to [`product-design.md`](./product-design.md) --- ## 1. Goals and constraints | Goal | Design consequence | | --- | --- | | Vim-fast UI | TUI never performs network I/O; it talks to a local daemon | | Agent-drivable | Stable JSON CLI + Unix-socket protocol; playback survives process exit | | Provider changes cheaply | All NetEase protocol knowledge behind one port + `ncmapi` | | Testable rules | Queue/state machine is pure, in `lekima-domain`; no I/O in tests | | Small blast radius | One writer of playback state; adapters are replaceable | | Safe by construction | `unsafe` forbidden in first-party crates; secrets off argv/logs; strings sanitized | Hard constraints: Rust 2024 edition, MSRV 1.98, macOS + Linux first-class, single static binary, no mandatory system audio libraries beyond what rodio needs (CoreAudio on macOS; ALSA/Pulse on Linux). ## 2. Context ```mermaid flowchart LR user([Human]) -->|keys| tui[lekima TUI] agent([Code agent / script]) -->|argv| cli[lekima CLI] tui -->|JSON-lines over UDS| daemon[(lekima daemon)] cli -->|JSON-lines over UDS| daemon daemon -->|HTTPS| ncm[(ncmapi-rs)] ncm --> netease[(NetEase Cloud Music)] daemon -->|rodio| audio[(Audio device)] daemon -->|cookies 0600| disk[(~/.config/lekima)] cli -->|spawn on demand| daemon ``` Deployment is a single container in the logical sense but two processes at runtime. The daemon is optional for read-only commands (`search`, `playlist show`, `lyrics`, `capabilities`, `doctor` talk to the provider directly). ## 3. Containers and crates ```mermaid flowchart TD cli[lekima-cli
binary: lekima] --> tui[lekima-tui] cli --> ipc[lekima-ipc] cli --> core[lekima-core] cli --> ncm[lekima-ncm] cli --> audio[lekima-audio] cli --> config[lekima-config] tui --> ipc tui --> domain[lekima-domain] core --> domain ncm --> domain audio --> domain config --> domain ipc --> domain ``` Dependency rule: **arrows point inward**. `lekima-domain` depends on nothing but `serde`, `thiserror`, `async-trait`. `lekima-core` may depend on domain only. Adapters depend inward. The CLI is the composition root — the only crate allowed to know every concrete type. | Crate | Responsibility | Must not | | --- | --- | --- | | `lekima-domain` | Entities, queue rules, playback state, ports | Do I/O, know HTTP/audio/terminal | | `lekima-core` | `Player`: queue + transport orchestration, auto-advance | Know about IPC or CLI | | `lekima-config` | Paths, `config.toml`, cookie file (0600) | Parse provider payloads | | `lekima-ipc` | Protocol types, UDS client/server framing | Contain business rules | | `lekima-ncm` | `MusicService` over `ncmapi` | Expose raw provider JSON | | `lekima-audio` | `AudioEngine` over rodio | Download catalogue metadata | | `lekima-tui` | Rendering, keymap, client-side state machine | Block on the network or own playback | | `lekima-cli` | Command parsing, daemon lifecycle, JSON rendering | Duplicate queue logic | Workspace layout: ``` lekima/ ├── Cargo.toml # workspace, resolver 3, shared versions ├── docs/ │ ├── product-design.md │ ├── system-design.md │ └── adr/ # architecture decision records ├── crates/ │ ├── lekima-domain/ │ ├── lekima-core/ │ ├── lekima-config/ │ ├── lekima-ipc/ │ ├── lekima-ncm/ │ ├── lekima-audio/ │ ├── lekima-tui/ │ └── lekima-cli/ # [[bin]] name = "lekima" └── tests/ # workspace-level integration tests ``` ## 4. Domain model Newtypes instead of raw integers (`TrackId`, `PlaylistId`, `UserId`, `AlbumId`, `ArtistId`). Prevents id mix-ups at compile time and gives a single place for validation. Serde is `transparent`, so the wire format stays `123`. ```mermaid classDiagram class Track { TrackId id; String name; Vec~Artist~ artists; Option~Album~ album; u64 duration_ms } class Artist { ArtistId id; String name } class Album { AlbumId id; String name; Option~String~ cover_url } class Playlist { PlaylistId id; String name; u64 track_count; Option~String~ owner } class UserProfile { UserId id; String nickname; Option~String~ avatar_url } class Queue { Vec~Track~ tracks; Option~usize~ current } class PlaybackState { PlaybackStatus status; Option~Track~ track; u64 position_ms; f32 volume; bool muted; RepeatMode repeat; bool shuffle } Queue --> Track PlaybackState --> Queue ``` Queue invariants (unit-tested in `lekima-domain`): - `current` is `None` iff `tracks` is empty; otherwise it is a valid index. - `advance(Off)` returns `None` at the tail and leaves the cursor unchanged; `advance(All)` wraps; `advance(One)` repeats. - `rewind` wraps only under `All`. - `remove_current` clamps the cursor; removing the last track empties the queue. ## 5. Playback state machine ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Stopped Stopped --> Playing: play(tracks) / URL resolved Playing --> Paused: pause() Paused --> Playing: resume() Playing --> Playing: track ends (advance) Playing --> Stopped: track ends, no next Playing --> Stopped: stop() Paused --> Stopped: stop() Stopped --> Playing: resume() with non-empty queue Playing --> Playing: seek()/volume() ``` `Player` is the **only** writer. Guarantees: - Transitions are serialized by a `tokio::sync::Mutex` around the inner state; the audio engine is called inside the critical section so observers never see “playing” before the sink is actually playing. - A failed URL resolution never leaves the machine in `Playing`. - `tick()` (called by the daemon every 500 ms) is the single place that reacts to end-of-track. No audio callback mutates application state. ## 6. Runtime architecture ### 6.1 Processes | Process | Lifetime | Responsibility | Concurrency | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Daemon (`lekima daemon run`, internal) | Long | Owns `Player`, provider session, socket listener | tokio multi-thread; one task per connection; one monitor task | | CLI | Short | Parse args, call provider or daemon, print | `#[tokio::main]` | | TUI | Session | Render, keymaps, call daemon | crossterm event thread + tokio client task | The TUI is **not** the player. Closing it does not stop the music; that is the whole point for agents and long coding sessions. ### 6.2 Daemon lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as lekima CLI participant L as lock file participant D as daemon C->>C: resolve socket path C->>D: connect + ping alt not running and autostart enabled C->>L: try lock (O_EXCL, 5 s budget) C->>D: spawn(binary, "daemon run", --foreground=false) D->>L: lock held by parent? wait for socket up (100 ms poll, 5 s) C->>D: ping end C->>D: command D-->>C: reply ``` - Socket: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/lekima.sock`, else `/cache/lekima.sock`; overridable with `LEKIMA_SOCKET`. - The socket directory is `0700`; the socket is `0600`. - Stale-socket handling: connection refused + existing file ⇒ unlink and retry once, after taking the startup lock. - Shutdown: `Shutdown` command or SIGTERM/SIGINT ⇒ stop audio, flush session, unlink socket. A `SIGKILL` leaves a stale socket that the next start reaps. - Single instance per socket path enforced with an advisory lock on `lekima.lock`. - Daemon logs to `/lekima.log` via `tracing` (daily-free, size-capped, one rotated previous file) and to stderr when run with `--foreground`. ### 6.3 TUI event loop ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant K as keyboard thread participant U as UI task participant I as IPC client task K->>U: Key(code, modifiers) U->>U: reduce(state, key) → Effect U->>I: Effect::Call(Command) I-->>U: Reply (or error toast) U->>U: draw(frame) loop every 500 ms while visible U->>I: Status (coalesced, one in flight) I-->>U: PlaybackState end ``` - Rendering is pure: `view(&App) -> Frame`. The `App` reducer is unit-testable without a terminal using `ratatui::backend::TestBackend`. - Network calls are fire-and-forget with request coalescing: a second `Status` request is skipped if one is in flight; key handling never awaits. - Terminal restore is guarded by a drop type + panic hook (raw mode, alternate screen, cursor visibility). ### 6.4 Audio pipeline ``` stream URL ── reqwest GET (UA + Referer, cookie) ──► bytes │ │ │ (v0.1) full body, capped by Content-Length │ └──────────────► rodio Decoder (symphonia) ──► Sink ──► OutputStream │ volume / pause / try_seek / empty() poll ``` Decisions: - **v0.1**: download the body fully before decoding. NetEase URLs are HTTP-range-capable but full download is the smallest correct implementation; `Content-Length` is checked against `LEKIMA_MAX_TRACK_BYTES` (default 64 MiB). - **v0.2**: progressive streaming via `reqwest::Response::bytes_stream()` into a bounded channel feeding `Decoder`. Enables instant start and seek on large lossless files. - Seek: `Sink::try_seek` when the decoder supports it; the UI additionally updates `position_ms` optimistically and reconciles on the next status poll. - Device errors (`NoDevice`, `DeviceBusy`) map to `ErrorCode::Playback` with a hint; `lekima doctor` enumerates devices. - The output stream is kept alive for the daemon’s lifetime; one sink per track, replaced on load (rodio mixes old/new, so we `stop` + drop before loading). ## 7. IPC protocol Line-delimited JSON over a Unix stream socket, one request per connection in v0.1 (connection-per-call; simple, robust, cheap at local latencies). ```jsonc // client → daemon {"id":1,"command":{"type":"play","target":{"type":"query","query":"mota"}}} // daemon → client {"id":1,"result":{"type":"status","state":{"status":"playing","track":{...},"position_ms":0}}} // daemon → client on failure {"id":1,"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"run `lekima login`"}} ``` Properties: - `MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 1 MiB`; oversized frames get one error and the connection closes (desynchronised streams are not recoverable). - Unknown fields are ignored by serde for forward compatibility; unknown command types produce `bad_request`. - `Response.id` echoes the request id. - **v0.2**: `hello` handshake advertising `protocol_version`; the client rejects mismatched majors with a clear message. Push events (`status_changed`, `queue_changed`) reuse the same framing with an `event` key instead of `id`. Security: - Socket permissions `0600`, parent directory `0700`. - On Linux, verify `SO_PEERCRED` uid matches the daemon owner; on macOS `getpeereid`. Reject otherwise. (Defence in depth; the socket mode already restricts access.) - No authentication tokens on the wire; the session stays inside the daemon. ## 8. Provider adapter (`lekima-ncm`) - `NcmMusicService` implements `MusicService` using `ncmapi::NcmClient`. - Constructed once per daemon; cookie path = `/session.cookies` (written by `lekima login`, `0600`). - Mapping layer owns all provider quirks: nested artists, missing album, `fee` flags, duration in ms, and `code != 200` handling. Mapping functions are pure and property-tested against fixtures. - Errors: HTTP/timeout ⇒ `Unavailable`; `code == 301` ⇒ `AuthenticationRequired`; empty result ⇒ `NotFound`; missing endpoint support ⇒ `Unsupported`. ### 8.1 Extending `ncmapi-rs` `ncmapi` 1.0 exposes only search, track metadata, stream URLs, account and user playlists. v0.1 works within that surface; v0.2 requires additions, released as `ncmapi 1.1`: | Endpoint | Route | Used by | | --- | --- | --- | | QR login start/poll | `/api/login/qrcode/unikey`, `/api/login/qrcode/client/login` | `lekima login --qr` | | Playlist detail with tracks | `/api/v6/playlist/detail` | `playlist show`, sidebar | | Lyrics | `/api/song/lyric` | lyrics pane | | Daily recommendations | `/api/v3/discover/recommend` | Daily section | | Personal FM | `/api/v1/radio/get` | FM section | | Like / unlike | `/api/radio/like` | track actions (`f`) | | Toplists | `/api/toplist` | sidebar | Process: develop with a path patch, add contract tests (wiremock fixtures), run the crate’s deterministic suite, bump minor version, publish, then pin `ncmapi = "1.1"` and delete the patch. Public API stays additive; the existing `NcmClient`/service shape is preserved. ## 9. Configuration `/config.toml`, parsed strictly (`deny_unknown_fields`) so typos fail loudly: ```toml [provider] cache = true cache_ttl_secs = 180 [playback] volume = 0.7 quality = "exhigh" # standard | higher | exhigh | lossless autoplay = true [ui] alternate_screen = true show_help_on_start = false [daemon] autostart = true log_level = "info" ``` Precedence: defaults → file → environment (`LEKIMA_CONFIG_DIR`, `LEKIMA_SOCKET`, `LEKIMA_LOG`, `LEKIMA_THEME`, `NO_COLOR`). Flags win over all. Files: `config.toml`, `session.cookies` (0600), `lekima.log`, `cache/` (response cache, future offline metadata). Nothing outside the root is written. ## 10. Error taxonomy and mapping | Domain error | IPC code | Exit | UX | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `InvalidInput` | `bad_request` | 2 | Inline usage hint | | `AuthenticationRequired` | `unauthorized` | 3 | “run `lekima login`” | | `NotFound` | `not_found` | 4 | “no matches for …” | | `Unsupported` | `unsupported` | 8 | “not available for this track” | | `Unavailable` | `backend` | 5 | Retry hint, provider status | | `Playback` | `playback` | 6 | Device hint + `doctor` | | IPC unreachable | `daemon` | 7 | Autostart hint | | Any other | `internal` | 1 | “this is a bug”, log path | Rules: adapters never construct user-facing prose with format-string injection from provider data; messages are structured and rendered by the frontend. ## 11. Observability - `tracing` spans: `ipc.request`, `player.play`, `ncm.request` (URL path only, never query payloads with cookies), `audio.load`. - Log levels via `RUST_LOG`; default `info`, `debug` adds state transitions, `trace` adds protocol frames with secrets redacted. - `lekima doctor --json` reports: version/build, socket path & reachability, daemon pid/uptime, session present (boolean, never the value), audio device, provider reachability, config file errors. - In-memory ring buffer (last 128 IPC calls) exposed by `daemon logs --json` for post-mortem without filesystem access. ## 12. Security & privacy 1. Session cookie is a bearer credential: file `0600`, directory `0700`, never in argv, never logged, redacted in error payloads, cleared by `logout`. 2. `lekima login` accepts stdin/file only (`--cookie-file -`), warns when a TTY is absent and stdin is empty. 3. Terminal injection: sanitize all provider strings (strip C0/C1, ESC, OSC/CSI, bidi overrides) before rendering or printing. Unit-tested with hostile fixtures. 4. No telemetry, no analytics, no phone-home. Provider requests go only to NetEase hosts. 5. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every first-party crate. 6. `cargo audit` / `cargo deny` in CI; dependency review before release. 7. Provider downloads are capped and never written to a user-visible library; caching is metadata-only. ## 13. Performance budgets | Metric | Budget | Measurement | | --- | --- | --- | | CLI cold start (`status`) | < 100 ms | hyperfine in CI benchmark | | Key → screen update | < 16 ms | `TestBackend` frame timing | | Daemon idle RSS | < 40 MB | CI on Linux | | Daemon RSS while playing | < 80 MB (128 kbps), < 200 MB (lossless, v0.1 full download) | manual | | Provider search | < 800 ms p50 | tracing histogram | | Socket round-trip | < 2 ms p99 local | tracing | | Status poll rate | 2 Hz idle, 4 Hz visible, 0 when TUI hidden | code review | ## 14. Testing strategy | Layer | Technique | | --- | --- | | Domain | Pure unit tests for queue/state edge cases; property tests for invariants | | Core | Fake `MusicService` + fake `AudioEngine`; transition and failure-injection tests | | NCM adapter | Fixture payloads → domain mapping; `wiremock` for transport errors; no live network in CI | | IPC | Encode/decode golden tests; server loop tests with `tokio::io::duplex` | | CLI | `assert_cmd` + `insta` snapshots for human and `--json` output; exit codes | | TUI | `TestBackend` snapshot + reducer tests (key sequences) | | E2E | Spawn daemon with fake provider + fake audio, drive CLI, assert JSON | | Faults | Corrupt cookie, socket removed mid-call, provider 5xx, oversized frame, SIGTERM | | CI | `fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, tests on macOS + Linux, `cargo deny` | Live-provider smoke tests are `#[ignore]` and run manually with a dedicated account. ## 15. Packaging & release - `cargo-dist` builds `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`. - Homebrew tap, `cargo install lekima`, GitHub Releases with checksums. - SemVer: protocol and CLI are public APIs. Breaking CLI/JSON change ⇒ major. - MSRV policy: latest stable; documented in `Cargo.toml`. - `ncmapi` releases are decoupled but listed in the changelog when a feature depends on a new version. ## 16. Architecture decision records | ADR | Decision | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | 001 | Daemon + thin clients | Playback outlives UIs; agents need stateless invocations | | 002 | Unix socket, JSON lines | Debuggable with `nc -U`, no schema compiler, forward compatible | | 003 | ratatui + crossterm | Actively maintained, testable `TestBackend`, standard choice | | 004 | rodio + symphonia | Pure-Rust decoding for mp3/aac/flac; no GStreamer dependency | | 005 | Newtype ids | Compile-time safety across five id kinds | | 006 | `ncmapi-rs` extended, not forked | Single client library, shared maintenance, published releases | | 007 | Cookie-file login first, QR second | Unblocks v0.1 without new endpoints; QR is the polished path | | 008 | Strict config parsing | Typos surface immediately instead of silently defaulting | | 009 | Full-download playback in v0.1 | Fewest moving parts; streaming behind the same port in v0.2 | | 010 | Poll status in v0.1, push events in v0.2 | Correctness first; protocol already supports unsolicited frames | ## 17. Failure modes | Scenario | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | Daemon dies mid-TUI | TUI shows “daemon lost”, retries connect every 2 s, offers `R` to restart | | Song URL 404/VIP | Toast, skip after 2 s (`--strict` stops instead) | | Audio device disappears | Playback error, state → Stopped, hint to run `doctor` | | Cookie expired | `unauthorized`, browsing still works, login hint | | Provider 5xx/timeout | `backend`, no state corruption; last track keeps playing | | Queue empty + `next` | `Ack`, state Stopped, exit 0 (not an error) | | Two daemons raced | Advisory lock; loser exits 0 with pid of winner | | TUI killed with SIGKILL | Terminal may be left in raw mode; `lekima doctor --fix` and `reset` documented | | Malformed provider JSON | Mapping returns `Unavailable`, never panics | ## 18. What exists today (honest status) Implemented and compiling: `lekima-domain` (model, queue, state, ports), `lekima-config` (paths, TOML, 0600 session file), `lekima-ipc` (protocol, client, server loop), `lekima-core` (`Player` with transition tests). Next: `lekima-ncm`, `lekima-audio`, daemon in `lekima-cli` (play/status/pause), then `lekima-tui`, then the agent surface (`capabilities`, JSON snapshots), then the `ncmapi-rs` 1.1 work.

# lekima

> NetEase Cloud Music in your terminal. Vim-first, agent-native.

`lekima` is a rewrite of the archived [benmooo/lekima](https://github.com/benmooo/lekima)
Go player as a layered Rust workspace. A small daemon owns playback; the TUI and
every CLI command are clients of the same local protocol, so music keeps playing
when you close the UI — and a code agent can drive it with one command.

```console
$ lekima play "bohemian rhapsody"
▶ Bohemian Rhapsody · Queen · A Night at the Opera   0:00 / 5:55

$ lekima status --json
{"ok":true,"data":{"status":"playing","track":{…},"volume":0.7}}
```

## Design documents

- [`docs/product-design.md`](docs/product-design.md) — users, principles, feature
  scope, keymap, agent contract, success criteria, milestones, risks.
- [`docs/system-design.md`](docs/system-design.md) — crate graph, playback state
  machine, daemon lifecycle, IPC protocol, provider adapter, security, testing,
  ADRs.

## Status

Early. The foundation (domain, configuration, IPC, player rules) is in place;
playback, TUI and the CLI surface are being implemented. The design documents
mark what is **now**, **next** and **later** — treat them as the plan of record.

## Workspace

| Crate | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `lekima-domain` | Entities, queue rules, playback state, ports. No I/O. |
| `lekima-core` | `Player`: orchestration and transitions. |
| `lekima-config` | Paths, `config.toml`, `0600` session storage. |
| `lekima-ipc` | JSON-lines protocol over a Unix socket. |
| `lekima-ncm` | `MusicService` adapter over [`ncmapi`](https://crates.io/crates/ncmapi). |
| `lekima-audio` | `AudioEngine` adapter over rodio. |
| `lekima-tui` | ratatui frontend. |
| `lekima-cli` | `lekima` binary and daemon. |

## Development

```bash
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all
```

Hermetic runs (no writes to your real config):

```bash
LEKIMA_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p lekima-cli -- status --json
```

## License

MIT. `lekima` is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with NetEase.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository.

## Read first

1. `docs/product-design.md` — what we are building and why.
2. `docs/system-design.md` — layering, crate boundaries, IPC, ADRs.
3. This file — conventions and commands.

## Non-negotiables

- **Dependency rule:** arrows point inward. `lekima-domain` must not gain I/O
  dependencies. Adapters depend on the domain, never the other way round. The
  CLI is the only composition root.
- **One writer:** only `lekima_core::Player` mutates playback/queue state. Never
  mutate state from a frontend or adapter.
- **No `unsafe`.** Every crate uses `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- **No secrets on argv or in logs.** Session cookies live in
  `<config>/session.cookies` with mode `0600` and are redacted anywhere they
  could be printed.
- **Sanitize provider text** before it reaches a terminal (C0/C1, CSI, OSC,
  bidi). Use the shared helper, never `println!` raw metadata.
- **Errors are typed.** Map to `DomainError`/`ErrorCode`; do not return strings
  from adapters. Frontends own user-facing prose.
- **Agent contract is public API:** command names, JSON fields, error codes and
  exit codes are versioned. Adding is fine; renaming is a major bump.

## Commands

```bash
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo deny check          # when touching dependencies
LEKIMA_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p lekima-cli -- status --json
```

## Code style

- Edition 2024, MSRV 1.98, `rustfmt` defaults; no `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside
  tests and `main` (use typed errors).
- Public items documented; docs explain *why*, tests explain *what*.
- Prefer newtypes over raw ids; prefer enums over booleans for modes.
- Keep pure logic in `lekima-domain`/`lekima-core` and cover it with tests. If a
  rule needs a socket or a device to test, it belongs in a frontend instead.
- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`).

## Adding a feature (checklist)

1. Model + rules in `lekima-domain` (unit tests).
2. Intent in `lekima-core::Player` (fake ports tests).
3. Provider call in `lekima-ncm` using an `ncmapi` endpoint; if it is missing,
   add it to `ncmapi-rs` with contract tests, release a minor, then bump.
4. Protocol command/reply in `lekima-ipc`.
5. CLI subcommand + JSON output + exit code; TUI key binding + hint.
6. Update `docs/product-design.md` (surface) and `docs/system-design.md`
   (protocol/ADR) if the contract changed.

# Sprint 2 — Product Design

> Theme: **Provider depth, live UI, agent-native control**
> Status: **Proposed** · Depends on: lekima 0.1 (sprint 1), ncmapi 1.1 (shipped)

Sprint 1 delivered the skeleton that matters: a daemon-owned player, a
keyboard-first TUI, a stable JSON CLI, and provider coverage for search,
playlists and lyrics. Sprint 2 closes the remaining feature gap with the
archived Go player and makes the experience feel finished rather than
functional.

---

## 1. Sprint goal

**A user can live in lekima for a full day without touching another player, and
an agent can drive every new action through the same stable contract.**

Concretely, at the end of this sprint:

- `lekima tui` opens on a **Home** view with Daily recommendations, Personal FM,
  Toplists and the liked playlist one key away.
- The now-playing bar updates **without polling** (sub-50 ms after a track
  changes, including changes initiated by another shell or agent).
- Lyrics are a **pane, not a command**: synced highlighting, translation toggle,
  offset adjustment, no layout breakage at small sizes.
- `lekima mcp` exposes the player as MCP tools so an agent can call `play`,
  `pause`, `next`, `search`, `status`, `lyrics` directly.
- Every new capability exists in three places with identical semantics: TUI key,
  CLI subcommand, JSON/event payload.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Job this sprint | Current pain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal developer | “Put on my daily mix and keep it going while I code.” | Daily/FM missing; must search manually |
| Long-session listener | “Show lyrics while a track plays, without leaving the queue.” | `lekima lyrics` replaces the screen and blocks |
| Agent operator | “React to track changes; keep a queue fed.” | The agent has to poll `status` every 500 ms |
| MCP-native agent | “Call the player as tools, not shell commands.” | No MCP server; shell quoting is brittle |
| Curator | “Like this track, and later find everything I liked.” | No like action, no liked list |

## 3. Principles carried forward

1. Keyboard first; every new feature gets a key and a hint.
2. One writer: only the daemon mutates state; UIs render events.
3. Stable agent contract: additive changes only within 0.x; error codes and exit
   codes are frozen.
4. Nothing blocks the UI thread; loading is a state, not a freeze.
5. Respect the provider: likes/FM/trash are user-initiated actions only, no
   background automation.

## 4. Scope

### 4.1 In scope

| # | Feature | Why now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S2-1 | Daily recommendations | The single most-used entry point in the old app |
| S2-2 | Personal FM (start, next, trash) | Original feature; also exercises infinite queues |
| S2-3 | Like / unlike + liked playlist | Small surface, high daily value |
| S2-4 | Toplists (list + detail) | Discovery without an account |
| S2-5 | Lyrics pane (synced, translated, offset) | Lyrics exist in the API; the pane is the missing UI |
| S2-6 | Daemon push events + `lekima watch` | Removes polling; enables agent reactions |
| S2-7 | MCP server (`lekima mcp`) | The explicit agent-native ask |
| S2-8 | Polish pass | Themes/`NO_COLOR`, counts, yank, loading states, hints |

### 4.2 Out of scope (sprint 3 candidates)

- Comments pane, cloud disk, downloads/offline library.
- MPRIS / macOS Now Playing, desktop notifications, scrobbling.
- Multi-account, social features, podcast/video.
- Windows named pipes (WSL + TCP localhost remain the story).

## 5. Feature specifications

### S2-1 Daily recommendations

**Story:** As a listener, I press `d` and get today's personalised list, already
playing.

- Source: `GET/POST /api/v3/discover/recommend` (weapi). Returns `recommend`
  (playlists), `dailySongs` and `recommendReasons`.
- Home view shows a **Daily** row with the first 5 tracks and “+N more”.
- `Enter` plays from the selected track to the end of the list.
- Cached for 30 minutes per account; `Ctrl-r` forces a refresh.
- Unauthenticated users see “Daily needs a session — `lekima login --qr`”
  instead of an error toast.
- CLI: `lekima daily [--limit N] [--json]`, `lekima play --daily`.

**Acceptance:** pressing `d` twice within 30 min does not refetch; the list is
stable across daemon restarts within the TTL; the JSON payload contains
`source: "daily"` so agents can tell queues apart.

### S2-2 Personal FM

**Story:** As a listener, I press `F` and get an endless, personalised station I
can steer with next/trash.

- Source: `/api/v1/radio/get` returns a batch (typically 3 tracks); `/api/radio/trash`
  removes the current track from the station.
- FM is a **queue mode**, not a playlist: when fewer than 2 tracks remain, the
  daemon prefetches the next batch in the background.
- `n` (next) skips without trashing. `x` in the FM pane **trashes** the current
  track and advances (confirm dialog, session-scoped undo).
- Leaving FM (playing anything else) ends the mode; the batch cache is kept for
  the session.
- Playback failure during FM skips after one retry and logs a structured event.
- CLI: `lekima fm start|next|trash|stop`, `lekima play --fm`.

**Acceptance:** 20 consecutive “next” presses never empty the queue while the
network is healthy; trash removes the track for the session and is never
re-added from the same batch; `lekima status` reports `queue.kind = "fm"`.

### S2-3 Like / unlike

**Story:** As a listener, `f` likes the current track; `f` again unlikes it.

- Source: `/api/radio/like?alg=itembased&trackId=<id>&like=<true|false>&time=3`.
- The track list shows a `♥` marker for liked tracks in Daily, FM, playlists and
  search results.
- State is **set-state**, not toggle, in the API: `lekima like --id 123 --value
  true`; the TUI toggles based on cached state.
- Optimistic UI: the marker flips immediately; on failure it rolls back and
  shows “couldn’t update like”.
- The liked set is cached per session (`/api/likelist?uid=…`) and invalidated on
  every successful change.
- `lekima liked [--json]` plays/lists the liked playlist.
- Requires a session; otherwise `unauthorized` with the login hint.

**Acceptance:** like → restart daemon → the marker is still correct; concurrent
likes from two clients converge (last write wins, no phantom toggles); the API
never receives a like action the user did not initiate.

### S2-4 Toplists

**Story:** As a listener, `t` opens the charts and `Enter` plays one.

- Source: `/api/toplist` (list) and existing playlist detail/paging for entries.
- Home sidebar section “Toplists” with the 8–12 official charts.
- Cached 15 minutes; no session required.
- CLI: `lekima toplist [list]`, `lekima toplist show <id> [--play]`.

**Acceptance:** works logged out; chart order matches the provider; opening a
chart never blocks the TUI (loading row shown).

### S2-5 Lyrics pane

**Story:** As a listener, `L` opens lyrics beside the queue and the current line
lights up.

- LRC parsing moves into `lekima-domain` as a pure value type:
  `Lyrics { lines: Vec<LyricLine { at: Duration, text: String }> }` plus optional
  translation per line.
- Pane layout: right column (40% width) on wide terminals; full-screen overlay on
  narrow ones (`< 100` cols).
- Current line is highlighted, auto-scrolled, with a 1-line look-ahead.
- `[` / `]` shift the offset by ±250 ms, persisted per track for the session.
- `t` inside the pane toggles translation; `w` wraps long lines.
- No lyrics ⇒ “No lyrics for this track” placeholder, pane stays open.
- Cached in memory (LRU, 64 tracks) and on disk under `cache/lyrics/` for 30
  days (plain text only, no account data).
- CLI: `lekima lyrics [--id ID] [--offset ±ms] [--translate] [--json]` returns both
  raw LRC and parsed lines.

**Acceptance:** parser handles metadata tags, multiple timestamps per line,
blank lines, translation-only lines; highlighting never drifts more than 250 ms
from the audio position over a 5-minute track; the pane does not reflow the
track table at 120×40.

### S2-6 Push events + `lekima watch`

**Story:** As an agent, I subscribe once and react to track changes without
polling.

- Protocol v2 adds `hello` (version negotiation), `subscribe` (`status`,
  `queue`, `track`, `likes`), `unsubscribe`, and unsolicited `event` frames.
- Coalescing: status events at most 4 Hz; queue/like events are immediate;
  every event carries a monotonically increasing `seq` and the last `seq` is
  replayable via `since`.
- Slow subscribers: status events are dropped (latest wins); state-bearing
  events are never dropped.
- TUI switches to `subscribe`; it falls back to 500 ms polling against a v1
  daemon (detected via `hello`).
- `lekima watch [--events status,queue] [--json]` prints NDJSON frames; exits on
  SIGINT. `--since <seq>` replays from the daemon’s ring buffer (last 256).
- Event payloads reuse the domain types (`PlaybackState`, `Track`) — no parallel
  schema.

**Acceptance:** a track change initiated by `lekima next` in another shell
reaches a watching agent in < 50 ms p99 locally; a stalled reader does not grow
daemon memory (ring buffer bounded); v1 clients keep working unchanged.

### S2-7 MCP server

**Story:** As an MCP-capable agent, I add `lekima mcp` and call player tools.

- `lekima mcp` speaks MCP over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0), starts no daemon of its own
  but connects to the existing socket (autostart allowed unless disabled).
- Tools: `player_status`, `search`, `play`, `pause`, `resume`, `next`, `previous`,
  `set_volume`, `queue_add`, `queue_list`, `lyrics`, `daily`, `fm`.
- Every tool returns the same JSON `data` payload as the CLI subcommand, plus a
  one-line `content` summary for chat UIs.
- Errors map to MCP `isError` with the stable error code in `structuredContent`.
- Read-only tools are advertised separately so hosts can auto-approve them.
- No secrets cross the MCP boundary; the server holds no session state.

**Acceptance:** `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` lists the tools; calling
`play` with a query produces audible playback and a JSON result; the server
survives a daemon restart (reconnects on the next call).

### S2-8 Polish

- Theme config: `dark` (default), `light`, `mono`, `NO_COLOR`.
- Vim counts: `5j`, `3G`; `gg`/`G`; `Ctrl-o`/`Ctrl-i` jump list (stretch).
- `y` yanks `title — artist  https://music.163.com/song?id=<id>` (ID when no URL).
- Loading/empty/error states for every pane; spinner in the header only.
- Hint bar becomes contextual per pane and mode.
- `lekima doctor` gains provider endpoint checks and cache sizes.

## 6. UX details

### 6.1 Home view

```
┌ library ───────┬ Home ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ Discover     │ Daily · Wednesday           5 tracks · 18 more          │
│   Daily (28)   │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│   Personal FM  │ ▶ Cigarettes and lighters · LoMo            1:49  ♥    │
│   Toplists     │   Mota · Russian Circles                    6:32  ♥    │
│ ▾ Mine         │   ...                                                  │
│   ♥ Liked (312)│                                                        │
│   Focus (42)   │ Toplists                                               │
│   Late night   │   1 热歌榜   2 新歌榜   3 飙升榜   4 原创榜           │
└────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 NORMAL  j/k move · ⏎ play · d daily · F fm · t toplists · f like · L lyrics
```

### 6.2 Keymap additions

| Key | Context | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `d` | Normal | Open Daily |
| `F` | Normal | Start Personal FM |
| `t` | Normal | Open Toplists |
| `f` | Normal (track) | Like / unlike current or selected |
| `L` | Normal | Toggle lyrics pane |
| `[` / `]` | Lyrics | Offset −250 / +250 ms |
| `t` | Lyrics | Toggle translation |
| `w` | Lyrics | Toggle wrap |
| `x` | FM | Trash current track (confirm) |
| `u` | FM | Undo last trash (session) |
| `5j`, `3G` | Normal | Count prefix |
| `y` | Normal | Yank track label + URL/ID |
| `Ctrl-r` | Normal | Refresh current section (bypass cache) |
| `Ctrl-o`/`Ctrl-i` | Normal | Jump back / forward (stretch) |

`:` commands: `daily`, `fm`, `like`, `liked`, `toplist [id]`, `lyrics`,
`watch`, `theme <name>`.

### 6.3 Pane routing

| Terminal width | Lyrics pane |
| --- | --- |
| ≥ 120 cols | Right column, 40%, queue stays visible |
| 100–119 | Right column, 32% |
| < 100 | Full-screen overlay (`L` toggles, `Esc` closes) |

## 7. Agent contract additions

New commands (all support `--json`):

```
lekima daily [--limit N]
lekima fm start|next|trash|stop
lekima like [--id ID | --current] [--value true|false]
lekima liked
lekima toplist [list] | lexima toplist show <ID> [--play]
lekima lyrics [--id ID] [--offset ±ms] [--translate]
lekima watch [--events status,queue,track,likes] [--since SEQ]
lekima mcp
```

Stable additions to JSON:

```jsonc
// status
{"ok":true,"data":{"status":"playing","queue":{"kind":"daily","length":28}, ...}}

// like
{"ok":true,"data":{"track_id":123,"liked":true}}

// watch (NDJSON, one frame per line)
{"seq":42,"event":{"type":"track_changed","track":{...}}}
```

Rules: `like` is idempotent set-state; `fm trash` is idempotent per
track+batch; `watch` exit code is 0 on SIGINT; new error code
`not_subscribed` is **not** introduced (unknown events are ignored).

## 8. Metrics and acceptance

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Event latency (daemon → subscriber, local) | p99 < 50 ms |
| FM “next” time to first audio | p95 < 800 ms (prefetched batch) |
| Lyrics highlight drift | < 250 ms over 5 min |
| TUI frame time with lyrics open | < 8 ms at 120×40 |
| Daily cache hit rate in a session | > 90% |
| Agent demo (MCP): play → status → next → volume | passes in CI harness |
| New JSON commands covered by contract tests | 100% |

## 9. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider endpoints change (daily/FM/like) | Features break | All routes isolated in ncmapi 1.2 + contract tests with fixtures; graceful `unsupported` |
| FM batch repeats | Feels broken | Dedupe by track id per session; trash-aware filtering |
| Event protocol drift | Agents break | Versioned `hello`; additive event types; golden protocol tests |
| Lyrics timing varies by source | Highlight drift | User offset; clamp; unit tests with real fixtures |
| MCP host quirks | Integration pain | Inspector-based integration test; minimal dependency surface |
| Scope creep (comments/downloads) | Slip | Explicitly out of scope |

## 10. Rollout

1. ncmapi 1.2 (daily, FM, like, toplist) published and pinned.
2. Daemon protocol v2 behind negotiation; v1 clients untouched.
3. TUI features behind keymap; no flag needed (additive).
4. `lekima watch` and `lekima mcp` documented with copy-paste examples.
5. Release 0.2.0 with a migration note: none required, all additive.

## 11. Open questions

1. Should `f` like the **playing** track or the **selected** track? Proposal:
   selected when the track list has focus, playing otherwise; show which in the
   hint bar.
2. Is `x`-to-trash on FM discoverable enough, or should trash live behind `:fm
   trash` only? Proposal: keep `x` with a confirm dialog and undo.
3. Lyrics translation: show side-by-side or replace the original? Proposal:
   replace with `t`, keep original in `data` for agents.
4. Should `lekima watch` be NDJSON by default even without `--json`? Proposal:
   yes — it is inherently machine output; humans read it through `jq`.
5. MCP tool naming: prefix with `lekima_`? Proposal: no prefix; the server is
   already namespaced by the host.

# Sprint 2 — System Design

> Companion to [`product-design.md`](./product-design.md).
> Scope: daily recommendations, Personal FM, like/unlike, toplists, lyrics pane,
> push events, MCP server, polish.

Status: **Proposed** · Builds on sprint 1 ([`../system-design.md`](../system-design.md))

---

## 1. Constraints and quality attributes

| Constraint | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Only the daemon mutates playback/queue | Every new action is a protocol command; UIs never write state |
| Existing v1 clients must keep working | Protocol v2 is negotiated; old framing stays valid |
| Agents need low-latency reactions | Push events with bounded, coalesced delivery |
| Provider surface is fragile | New routes confined to `ncmapi` 1.2 with contract tests |
| TUI must stay at 60 fps | No I/O in the render loop; events mutate a view model |
| No secrets off-device | Likes/FM only on explicit user action; no telemetry |

Performance budgets: event latency p99 < 50 ms, lyrics parse < 5 ms for a
10-minute track, FM prefetch when ≤ 2 tracks remain, cache memory < 8 MB.

## 2. Changes at a glance

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph ncmapi 1.2
    D[discovery: daily, toplists]
    R[radio: fm, trash, like, likelist]
  end
  subgraph lekima-domain
    DM[models: Lyrics, LyricLine, QueueKind, LikeState]
    EV[event: PlayerEvent, Seq]
    PT[ports: DiscoveryService extensions]
  end
  subgraph lekima-core
    P[Player: FM mode, like cache]
    B[EventBus: broadcast]
  end
  subgraph lekima-ipc
    V2[protocol v2: hello/subscribe/event]
  end
  subgraph frontends
    TUI[TUI: Home panes, lyrics pane, event subscriber]
    CLI[CLI: daily/fm/like/toplist/watch/mcp]
    MCP[MCP stdio server]
  end
  ncmapi 1.2 --> lekima-ncm
  lekima-ncm --> PT
  PT --> P
  P --> B --> V2 --> TUI
  V2 --> CLI
  CLI --> MCP
  DM --> P
  EV --> B
```

### 2.1 New/changed crates

| Crate | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `lekima-domain` | `Lyrics`/`LyricLine`, `QueueKind`, `LikeState`, `PlayerEvent`, `seq`; new port methods for daily/FM/toplists/like |
| `lekima-core` | FM queue mode + prefetch, like cache + optimistic rollback, `EventBus`, event emission on every transition |
| `lekima-ncm` | Map daily/FM/toplist/like payloads; typed lyrics with timings |
| `lekima-ipc` | Protocol v2: `Hello`, `Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `Event` frames, `seq`, ring buffer |
| `lekima-tui` | Home view, section router, lyrics pane + LRC parser use, subscriber loop, counts, yank |
| `lekima-cli` | New subcommands, `watch`, `mcp` server, event rendering |
| `ncmapi` (1.2) | Routes + models + services for the four new areas |

## 3. Provider layer (`ncmapi` 1.2)

### 3.1 Routes and signatures

| Area | Route | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Daily | `POST /api/v3/discover/recommend` | `discovery().daily() -> ApiResponse<DailyBody>` | Requires session; `dailySongs`, `recommendReasons` |
| FM | `POST /api/v1/radio/get` | `radio().fm_batch() -> ApiResponse<FmBody>` | Returns 3–5 tracks |
| FM trash | `POST /api/radio/trash` | `radio().trash(id)` | Session-scoped removal |
| Like | `POST /api/radio/like` | `radio().set_like(id, bool)` | `alg=itembased`, `time=3` |
| Liked ids | `POST /api/likelist` | `radio().liked_ids(user)` | Used to seed the cache |
| Toplists | `POST /api/toplist` | `discovery().toplists()` | No session needed |

Models keep provider names (`dailySongs`, `recommendReasons`, `data`) in
`ncmapi`; the adapter maps them to domain names, so provider renames never leak
into lekima.

### 3.2 Error and edge behaviour

- `code == 301` ⇒ `AuthenticationRequired` for daily/FM/like; toplists stay
  public.
- Empty FM batch with `code == 200` ⇒ `NotFound("fm exhausted")`; the core treats
  it as “station empty for now” and retries once after 2 s.
- Like endpoint returns `{code: 200, data: ...}`; a non-200 body code maps to
  `Unavailable` and triggers optimistic rollback.
- Rate limits: no automatic retries for likes/trash (user intent must not be
  duplicated); read endpoints may retry once with jitter.

### 3.3 Versioning

`ncmapi 1.1` is published (tag `v1.1.0`). Sprint 2 adds `1.2.0`: purely
additive services/models. Steps: contract tests (wiremock fixtures + stub
transport), `cargo publish --dry-run`, tag, publish, then bump lekima’s pin and
remove any patch. MSRV unchanged.

## 4. Domain model additions

```rust
pub struct LyricLine {
    pub at: Duration,
    pub text: String,
    pub translation: Option<String>,
}

pub struct Lyrics {
    pub lines: Vec<LyricLine>,      // sorted by `at`
    pub offset: Duration,           // user adjustment, applied at render
    pub raw: String,                // original LRC for agents
}

pub enum QueueKind { Manual, Daily, Fm, Toplist, Playlist(PlaylistId), Liked }

pub struct LikeState {
    pub track: TrackId,
    pub liked: bool,
    pub pending: bool,              // optimistic write in flight
}

pub enum PlayerEvent {
    TrackChanged { track: Option<Track>, queue: QueueKind },
    StatusChanged { state: PlaybackState },
    QueueChanged { tracks: Vec<Track>, index: Option<usize>, kind: QueueKind },
    LikeChanged { track: TrackId, liked: bool },
    FmBatchLoaded { count: usize },
    Error { code: ErrorCode, message: String },
}
```

Invariants:

- `Lyrics.lines` is sorted and deduplicated by timestamp; `offset` never moves
  a line before zero when applied.
- `QueueKind::Fm` is the only kind that may grow without bound; it is capped at
  200 queued tracks (oldest played tracks are dropped).
- `LikeState.pending` is never persisted; it exists only in the daemon.

The LRC parser is pure and lives in `lekima-domain::lyrics`:

```rust
pub fn parse_lrc(raw: &str, translation: Option<&str>) -> Lyrics
```

Rules: tag lines (`[ar:]`, `[ti:]`, `[by:]`, `[offset:]`) are metadata; multiple
timestamps per line duplicate the text; `[mm:ss.xx]` and `[mm:ss.xxx]` supported;
`[offset:+ms]` is applied at parse time; empty text lines are skipped; unparsable
lines are preserved as untimed text at the end (never dropped).

## 5. Core changes

### 5.1 Queue modes

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Manual
  Manual --> Daily: play daily
  Daily --> Fm: start fm
  Fm --> Fm: prefetch when remaining <= 2
  Fm --> Manual: play something else / stop
  Daily --> Playlist: open playlist
  Playlist --> Toplist: open chart
  any --> Idle: stop + clear
```

`Player` gains:

```rust
pub async fn play_daily(&self) -> Result<PlaybackState>;
pub async fn fm_start(&self) -> Result<PlaybackState>;
pub async fn fm_next(&self, trash: bool) -> Result<Option<Track>>;
pub async fn fm_stop(&self) -> Result<()>;
pub async fn set_like(&self, id: TrackId, liked: bool) -> Result<bool>;
```

FM prefetch runs as a daemon task holding a weak reference to the player:

- Trigger: after any advance, `remaining <= 2` and kind is FM.
- Guard: one in-flight prefetch (`AtomicBool`), dedupe ids against the live
  batch and a `HashSet<TrackId>` of trashed tracks.
- Failure: emit `PlayerEvent::Error`, retry with exponential backoff (2 s, 4 s,
  8 s, cap 30 s), never block playback.

Like cache:

- `HashMap<TrackId, bool>` seeded from `liked_ids` on login/first use.
- `set_like`: optimistic insert with `pending=true` → provider call → confirm or
  rollback + event.
- Serialised per track with a small mutex map so double-presses cannot race.

### 5.2 Event bus

```rust
pub struct EventBus {
    sender: broadcast::Sender<SequencedEvent>,
    ring: Mutex<VecDeque<SequencedEvent>>, // last 256
    seq: AtomicU64,
}
```

- Every mutation calls `bus.publish(event)` **after** state is committed.
- `publish` assigns `seq`, appends to the ring, then broadcasts (lagging
  receivers drop status events; state events are reconstructed from the ring on
  resubscribe).
- Ordering guarantee: per-process total order by `seq`. Clients may detect gaps
  and resync with `Status`/`Queue`.

## 6. IPC protocol v2

### 6.1 Handshake

```jsonc
// client → daemon
{"id":1,"command":{"type":"hello","protocol":2}}
// daemon → client
{"id":1,"result":{"type":"welcome","protocol":2,"seq":128,"capabilities":["events","fm","daily","like","toplists"]}}
```

Rules:

- A v2 daemon accepts v1 commands unchanged (no `hello` required).
- A v2 client against a v1 daemon receives `bad_request` for `hello`; it must
  fall back to polling and disable event-only UX.
- `capabilities` is the source of truth for feature discovery; `capabilities`
  CLI command merges daemon capabilities with the static command catalogue.

### 6.2 Subscription and events

```jsonc
{"id":2,"command":{"type":"subscribe","events":["status","queue","track","likes"],"since":128}}
{"id":2,"result":{"type":"subscribed","since":128}}
{"event":{"seq":129,"type":"track_changed","track":{…},"queue":"fm"}}
{"event":{"seq":130,"type":"status_changed","state":{…}}}
```

Transport: the subscribing connection switches from request/reply to
bidirectional framing. Replies to new commands on the same connection carry
`id`; events carry `seq` and no `id`. A single writer per connection (daemon
task) guarantees no interleaving.

Backpressure policy:

| Event | Policy |
| --- | --- |
| `status_changed` | Coalesce to latest at 4 Hz; drop if the outgoing queue is full |
| `track_changed`, `queue_changed`, `like_changed` | Bounded queue (64); if full, drop the connection and mark it stale (client resubscribes with `since`) |
| `error` | Never dropped |

Ring buffer: 256 sequenced events. `subscribe {since}`:
- `since >= ring.first().seq` and `since <= last` ⇒ replay gap, then live.
- `since < ring.first().seq` ⇒ `subscribed` with `resync: true`; client must call
  `Status` and `Queue` before trusting the stream.

### 6.3 Watch client

```text
lekima watch --events status,queue --since 120 --json
```

- Connects, `hello`, `subscribe`, then copies event frames to stdout as NDJSON.
- Aggregates nothing; exit 0 on SIGINT/SIGTERM; exit 7 if the daemon is
  unreachable (no autostart for watch — an agent should know).
- Reconnects with exponential backoff (250 ms → 5 s) unless `--once` is given.

## 7. TUI architecture changes

### 7.1 View model

```rust
pub struct App {
    pub route: Route,             // Home, Tracks{source}, Queue, Help, Lyrics
    pub home: HomeSections,       // daily, toplists, liked, playlists
    pub lyrics: LyricsView,       // Option<Lyrics>, scroll, offset
    pub liked: HashSet<TrackId>,
    pub counts: CountPrefix,      // pending digits for vim counts
    pub subscription: SubscriptionState,
    ...
    pub events: EventStream,      // subscriber / poll fallback
}
```

Reducer stays pure: `KeyEvent × App → Action`; events are folded in `apply`.
Rendering reads only `App`.

### 7.2 Event-driven loop

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant K as keys
  participant R as reducer
  participant S as subscriber task
  participant D as daemon
  R->>S: Subscribe(status,queue,track,likes)
  S->>D: hello + subscribe(since)
  D-->>S: event(seq=n)
  S-->>R: PlayerEvent
  R->>R: apply → App state
  R->>R: draw
  Note over R,S: status ticks only in fallback mode
```

- One long-lived connection, owned by a task; reconnect with resubscribe.
- Coalescing on the UI side: at most one redraw per event batch (drain the
  channel before drawing).
- Fallback (v1 daemon): the existing 250 ms status poll + on-demand queue
  refresh, flagged in the footer (“polling”).

### 7.3 Lyrics pane

- Parsing: `lekima-domain::lyrics::parse_lrc` in the IPC reply (the daemon
  returns parsed lines + raw text). The TUI never parses provider data.
- Highlight selection: `partition_point` over sorted timestamps, O(log n) per
  frame.
- Layout: `Layout` splits at ≥100 cols; otherwise overlay. The queue table gets
  `Constraint::Min(40)` so it never collapses below usability.
- Scroll: keep the active line at 40% height; manual scroll pauses auto-scroll
  until the next track (or `g`).

### 7.4 Home sections and caching

- Each section has `Idle | Loading | Ready(ts) | Failed`.
- TTLs: daily 30 min, toplists 15 min, liked 5 min (invalidated on like).
- `Ctrl-r` forces refresh of the focused section.
- Rendering a `Loading` section shows one skeleton row with the section title,
  never a blank pane.

## 8. MCP server

### 8.1 Process model

```
agent host ──stdio JSON-RPC──> lekima mcp ──UDS protocol v2──> daemon
```

- `lekima mcp` is a thin adapter: no playback, no cache, no session.
- On start: `initialize` → `tools/list`; it does not touch the daemon until the
  first tool call.
- On daemon loss: tool call returns an MCP error `isError: true` with
  `structuredContent.error.code = "daemon"`; next call retries the connection.
- Stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC; logs go to stderr; `RUST_LOG` honoured.
- Shutdown: SIGTERM/EOF on stdin ⇒ exit 0.

### 8.2 Tool mapping

| Tool | IPC command | Result data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `player_status` | `Status` | `PlaybackState` |
| `search` | `Search` | `SearchResults` |
| `play` | `Play { Query/Tracks/Playlist }` | `PlaybackState` |
| `pause` / `resume` | `Pause`/`Resume` | `PlaybackState` |
| `next` / `previous` | `Next`/`Prev` | `PlaybackState` |
| `set_volume` | `SetVolume` | `PlaybackState` |
| `queue_add` | `Enqueue` | `Ack` + queue |
| `queue_list` | `Queue` | `Queue` |
| `lyrics` | `Lyrics` | `Lyrics` |
| `daily` | `Play { Daily }` | `PlaybackState` |
| `fm` | `FmStart`/`FmNext` | `PlaybackState` |

Tool schemas reuse the serde shapes; `content` is `"Playing Mota — Russian
Circles"` so chat UIs have something to say. Read-only tools are `player_status`,
`search`, `queue_list`, `lyrics`.

### 8.3 Safety

- No tool can read the session file; no tool takes a cookie/token argument.
- `play` with a free-form query performs its own search; it cannot execute shell
  commands.
- The server refuses to start a daemon when `daemon.autostart = false`.

## 9. Caching and storage

| Data | Store | TTL | Bound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Daily list | in-memory | 30 min / per user | 1 entry |
| Toplists | in-memory | 15 min | 1 entry |
| Liked ids | in-memory | session | 50k ids |
| FM batch | in-memory | session | 200 tracks |
| Lyrics | memory LRU + disk | 30 days | 64 entries / 20 MB disk |
| Event ring | in-memory | n/a | 256 events |

Disk layout: `cache/lyrics/<track-id>.json` (`0600`, plain text only). No
account identifiers in filenames or contents.

## 10. Failure modes

| Scenario | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Daily/FM needs session | `unauthorized` + login hint; Home shows the hint inline |
| FM batch empty | retry once after 2 s; then “station empty”, playback stops cleanly |
| FM track fails to resolve | skip after one retry, emit `error` event, continue |
| Like call fails | optimistic marker rolls back, toast + event |
| Translation missing | original text only; `data.translation` omitted |
| Lyrics load fails | pane shows error with `r` retry; playback unaffected |
| Subscriber is slow | status events dropped, state events close the connection and force resync |
| v1 daemon | TUI falls back to polling; new commands return `bad_request` and the CLI explains |
| Daemon restarts while watching | client reconnects with `since=last_seq`; on `resync` it fetches status/queue |
| MCP host sends unknown tool | JSON-RPC error, server stays alive |

## 11. Testing strategy

| Area | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| ncmapi 1.2 | Stub-transport contract tests per route; wiremock for HTTP errors; fixtures for daily/FM/toplist/like |
| LRC parser | Table-driven: tags, multi-timestamp, offset, malformed, translation merge, ordering, fuzz for no panic |
| Core FM | Fake providers: prefetch threshold, dedupe, trash, retry/backoff, cap at 200 |
| Likes | Optimistic success/failure, concurrent double-press, cache seeding |
| Events | Sequence monotonicity, ring replay, gap resync, slow-subscriber policy |
| Protocol v2 | Golden frames, v1 compatibility matrix, subscribe/unsubscribe, `since` replay |
| TUI | Render snapshots for Home/lyrics (wide/narrow), reducer tests for counts/yank, no I/O in render |
| CLI | Contract tests for new commands, `watch` NDJSON stream, exit codes |
| MCP | stdio integration test with initialize/tools/list/call/error; inspector smoke |
| E2E | Fake provider + fake audio daemon; drive CLI and TUI reducer; assert events order |

## 12. Rollout plan

1. `ncmapi 1.2.0` branch → contract tests → dry-run → tag → publish → pin.
2. Domain/lyrics + events in `lekima-domain` (pure, tests first).
3. Core FM/likes/event bus; daemon wires the bus and v2 protocol.
4. TUI Home + subscriber + lyrics pane; fallback path tested against a v1 fake.
5. CLI commands + `watch` + `mcp`.
6. Polish (themes, counts, yank).
7. Release `lekima 0.2.0`; docs and README updated.

Each step is shippable behind a working v1 path; no flag day.

## 13. ADRs for this sprint

| ADR | Decision | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 011 | Push events, coalesced, sequenced, ring-buffered | Removes polling without unbounded memory or lost state |
| 012 | Protocol v2 negotiated in-band | One socket, no duplicate server, v1 clients unaffected |
| 013 | FM is a queue mode with prefetch | Infinite station semantics without a second player |
| 014 | LRC parsing in the domain, daemon returns parsed lines | UIs stay pure; one parser to test |
| 015 | MCP as a stdio adapter over IPC | No second state ownership; reuses the agent contract |
| 016 | Likes are optimistic with rollback | Keeps the TUI instant without lying about persisted state |

## 14. Work breakdown

| # | Task | Depends on | Definition of done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ncmapi 1.2 routes/models/services + tests | — | 1.2 dry-run passes, published |
| 2 | LRC parser + fixtures | — | 100% table cases + fuzz |
| 3 | Domain types for queues/events/likes | 2 | `cargo test` green |
| 4 | Core FM + prefetch + retries | 1,3 | Fake-provider tests |
| 5 | Like cache + optimistic flow | 1,3 | Concurrency tests |
| 6 | Event bus + ring buffer | 3 | Ordering/replay tests |
| 7 | IPC v2 hello/subscribe/events | 6 | Golden frames, v1 compat |
| 8 | Daemon wiring + capabilities | 4,5,7 | E2E fake-provider test |
| 9 | TUI Home sections | 1,8 | Snapshots |
| 10 | TUI lyrics pane | 2,8 | Snapshots at 3 widths |
| 11 | TUI subscriber + fallback | 7 | Fallback test with v1 fake |
| 12 | CLI daily/fm/like/toplist/lyrics | 8 | Contract tests |
| 13 | `watch` NDJSON | 7 | Stream test + reconnect |
| 14 | MCP server | 8 | Inspector smoke + stdio tests |
| 15 | Polish (themes, counts, yank) | 9 | Snapshot + docs |
| 16 | Docs, release 0.2.0 | all | Publish checklist |

## 15. Open technical questions

1. Should the daemon persist `liked` ids to disk for offline markers? Proposal:
   no in 0.2; refetch per session (privacy, simplicity).
2. Should lyrics disk cache be shared across accounts? Proposal: key by track id
   only; lyrics are public data.
3. Does `watch --since` need long replay (hours)? Proposal: no; ring is 256, and
   resync is the fallback.
4. Can `subscribe` be multiplexed per event type on one connection? Proposal:
   yes via `unsubscribe`; the daemon tracks a per-connection set.
5. MCP transport: stdio only, or also SSE for remote hosts? Proposal: stdio in
   0.2; document a `socat` bridge for the curious.
